clue.text: Lectures on ethnicity in Doncaster, for example?

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece set on another follows it

parts.note: a race is a group sharing ethnicity
a course is a series of lectures

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a lecture series about ethnicity is being held in a Yorkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Doncaster is a town, but here it stands for its famous horse-racing track, home of the St Leger.
explanation.definitionFit: Doncaster is an example of a venue where horses run in races; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Simple floating structure right behind

parts.note: aft means towards the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A basic float sits just at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Logs or planks lashed together to make a basic platform on water.

clue.text: Craft product one beat, commonly, when short of time

indicators.note: short of means missing, so the letter for time is removed

parts.note: a crotchet is the British name for a quarter note, one beat in common time

explanation.surface: A craftsman's piece is one beat behind when time runs short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' points to common time, where a crotchet (the British term for a quarter note) is one beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Needlework made by looping yarn with a hooked needle, an example of handicraft.

clue.text: Insect raising goose-pimples over Sussex town, say

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece over another comes first

parts.note: something creepy makes your flesh crawl

indicators.note: say means the town's name is used for its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: Crawley is a town in West Sussex, near Gatwick airport

explanation.surface: A bug that gives you goosebumps lives above a Sussex town.
explanation.walkthrough: CRAWLEY is a town in West Sussex, England; 'say' keeps only its sound.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal name for any bug or small crawling invertebrate.

clue.text: No longer bound to switch members at heart of team

indicators.note: switching members at the heart means two letters in the middle of the team's name trade places

parts.note: United is a name of many football teams, such as Manchester United

explanation.surface: A player, now free, swaps the central figures of a side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch members at heart of' swaps the middle I and T of UNITED.
explanation.definitionFit: Released from ropes or ties, so free.

clue.text: Full of menace, like a love-child's bar?

definitions.meaning: in heraldry the bar ... (strictly a bend or baton) marks illegitimacy

explanation.surface: A threatening, illegitimate child at a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The bar is not a pub but the heraldic 'bar sinister', said to mark an illegitimate line.
explanation.definitionFit: Means threatening, and is also the heraldic term for the left side, as in the bar sinister of a bastard's arms.

clue.text: Almost broke cover

indicators.note: almost tells us to stop one letter short of the full word for broke

parts.note: skint is British slang for having no money

explanation.surface: Someone nearly penniless blows their disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINT is everyday British slang for penniless; 'Almost' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as nouns: an outer layer or covering, as on fruit or a drum.

clue.text: Person who's crucial in supporting family doctor

indicators.note: in a down answer, a supporting piece goes underneath

parts.note: kin means family
GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor

explanation.surface: A key person backing the local GP.
explanation.definitionFit: The most important person in a group, on whom everything depends, like the central pin in skittles.

clue.text: Unsporting description of all but one type of insect

definitions.meaning: an idiom for unfair or against the spirit of the game

definitions.text: description of all but one type of insect
definitions.meaning: every insect but one kind can be described as not being that chirping one

explanation.surface: An entomologist's unsporting remark about insects.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase is true of every insect except the chirping one named in it.
explanation.definitionFit: An English idiom for unfair play, from the gentlemanly ideals of the bat-and-ball game.

clue.text: Book on folk traditions in excellent Italian

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the word for excellent

parts.note: fine means excellent

indicators.note: in an across answer, the book set on the folk traditions comes after them

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge handed down among a people
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A book about folklore written in very good Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' tempts as the definition of a novel title, but Book is the New Testament abbreviation, and 'in' wraps 'excellent' round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective for someone or something from Florence, an Italian city.

clue.text: Sucker (if female) given scent from the East

indicators.note: in an across answer, coming from the East means read right to left

parts.note: a tang is a sharp smell

explanation.surface: A female bloodsucker picks up a smell drifting in from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: Only female gnats bite and suck blood, so the bracketed '(if female)' makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Female insects of this kind suck blood from their victims, making them suckers in the literal sense.

clue.text: Hollow-faced judge stunned by source of illumination

parts.note: a lantern gives light
awed means struck with amazement

explanation.surface: A gaunt judge is dazzled by a light.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a long, thin jaw and sunken cheeks, a gaunt look.

clue.text: Nonentity setting bad-tempered dog on thief?

indicators.note: in an across answer, the dog set on the thief follows it

parts.note: to whip is slang for to steal, so a whipper is a thief
a snapper is a dog that snaps

explanation.surface: A worthless person sets a vicious dog on a burglar.
explanation.definitionFit: An impertinent, insignificant young person; a cheeky nobody.

clue.text: I contort in agonising repentance

indicators.note: agonising suggests writhing, so the letters of I contort in twist into a new order

explanation.surface: A penitent describes twisting in agony.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere remorse for wrongdoing; sorrow for sin.

clue.text: Science teacher originally appearing in old films

indicators.note: appearing in puts that letter inside the word for films

parts.note: pics is informal for pictures, i.e. films

indicators.note: originally means take the opening letter of teacher

explanation.surface: A science teacher used to feature in vintage films.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of 'teacher' goes inside PICS, after O for old.
explanation.definitionFit: The branch of physics dealing with light and vision.

clue.text: German cutie not subjected to abuse

indicators.note: abuse here means mistreat, so the letters of cutie and not are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A German girl who has not been mistreated.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective for the Germanic peoples, often used loosely to mean German.

clue.text: Tracery one in service raised in relief, perhaps

indicators.note: in puts the turned soldier inside the shuffled letters
perhaps says the letters of relief may be arranged otherwise
in a down answer, raised means read from the bottom up

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier, one in the services

explanation.surface: Ornamental stonework with a serviceman carved in relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the letters of 'relief' to FILREE; 'raised' turns the soldier upside down before 'in' sets him inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicate lacelike ornamental metalwork, a kind of fine tracery.

clue.text: Chap visiting continent with head of this state

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of this

parts.note: the word this

indicators.note: visiting puts the chap inside the continent

parts.note: Asia is a continent
man means a chap

explanation.surface: A man touring Asia with the leader of this state.
explanation.definitionFit: The island state of Australia lying south of the mainland.

clue.text: Notice woman on phone surrounded by water

indicators.note: on the phone we only hear words, so the pieces are taken by sound

parts.note: see means notice; Gert is a short form of the woman's name Gertrude

explanation.surface: Spotting a woman talking on the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic word for ringed by the sea, as an island is.

clue.text: Much-decorated men dined with knight on board

indicators.note: on board means carried inside, so the knight sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: OR is the Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers
ate means dined
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: Highly decorated servicemen ate with a knight aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is a crossword convention for ordinary soldiers, and N is the chess knight; 'on board' means carried within.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborately adorned, with lots of decoration.

clue.text: Solitary article thus securing DI's rise

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: securing means holding, so the Latin word wraps round the detective

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus

indicators.note: in a down answer, rise means read from the bottom up

parts.note: a DI, Detective Inspector, is a tec, slang for detective

explanation.surface: A lonely piece of writing that ensures a detective's promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: A DI is a Detective Inspector, so 'DI's' stands for a detective in general; 'rise' turns that word upward to CET, and 'securing' holds it within the Latin word.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit or monk living alone in self-denial; a recluse.

clue.text: Moor associated with Holmes's last case

indicators.note: last means the final letter of Holmes

parts.note: a heath is open moorland

explanation.surface: A moorland tied to Sherlock Holmes's final mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like a detective's investigation but is a cover for a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting cover, as for a sword or knife.

clue.text: Selfish comment every Tory read in introduction from London?

indicators.note: read in means entered into, as data is read into a record, so these words go inside

parts.note: a Londoner might introduce himself as I'm Jack, Jack being the stock name of the cheeky Cockney
all means every
Tories are on the political right

explanation.surface: A selfish remark made by a Conservative reading out a London introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read in' means entered into a record, so the words for every Tory go inside how a Cockney might introduce himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchphrase for complacent self-interest: as long as the speaker is comfortable, others can fend for themselves.

clue.text: Gold leaf regularly brought up for examination

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: in a down answer, brought up means read from the bottom up
regularly means take alternate letters of leaf

explanation.surface: Gold leaf is routinely presented for inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes L and A from 'leaf'; 'brought up' turns them to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test, as in a viva or language exam.

clue.text: Woman who keeps pupil in?

definitions.meaning: the coloured ring of the eye that surrounds its pupil

explanation.surface: A woman who gives a schoolchild detention.
explanation.walkthrough: The pupil is not a schoolchild but the opening at the centre of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, and the part of the eye that rings the dark central pupil.

clue.text: Mole's opportunity to engage at first in combat

parts.note: a break is a chance or opening

indicators.note: in places those letters inside the word for combat

parts.note: war is combat

indicators.note: at first means take the opening letters of to and engage

explanation.surface: A burrowing animal gets its chance to join the fighting early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' is not the animal but a stone pier; 'at first' takes T and E, which go inside WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a harbour wall or pier that shelters boats from waves.

clue.text: Military alliance in action at Oxford?

indicators.note: in shows the answer is tucked inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A military alliance goes into action at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a defence pact of Western nations.

clue.text: Orderly nonetheless admitted to health check

indicators.note: admitted to means let inside the word for health check

parts.note: a medical is a physical examination
tho is a short spelling of though, meaning nonetheless

explanation.surface: A hospital orderly is still allowed in for a checkup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orderly' looks like a hospital worker but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in a systematic, well-organised way.
